question: Why do network television dramas build a small cliffhanger roughly every ten to fifteen minutes?
answer: Because each act ends at an advert break. A network hour is cut into several acts, and writers end every one on a question so viewers stay through the adverts instead of changing channel. Series written for streaming, with no breaks, often drop these regular mini-cliffhangers and save one large hook for the end.
move: Look at where the pauses fall to see who the story serves.
ask: Where in my day do I get hooked into staying longer than I planned?
source: Douglas, Writing the TV Drama Series, 2005
reference: Pamela Douglas, Writing the TV Drama Series, Michael Wiese Productions, 2005
